panel.name: ScrapeTools benchmark panel, November 2026
panel.about: Fixed before the first run and not changed after seeing results. Each page has a category and one or more success markers: text a person sees on the page in a normal browser. A request succeeds only when every marker appears in the returned content and no block-page phrase does. Markers are matched case-sensitively after removing Markdown emphasis characters (* _ `) and collapsing whitespace. Practice sites are pages built to be scraped; their owners are named where the site names them.

categories.static: The content is in the page's HTML; a plain HTTP request gets it.
categories.js: The content is added by JavaScript after the page loads; a plain HTTP request does not get it.
categories.protected: A bot-protection challenge (Cloudflare) answers a plain HTTP request with 403 'Just a moment...'. Both pages are on a practice site that lists them as challenges to bypass. Reported separately from the general success rate, as the method says.

block_phrases: Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue

run_plan.order: Pages are interleaved by host, the same order every round; one request at a time.
run_plan.pacing: At least 8 seconds between request starts (under the free plan's 10 scrapes a minute), and at least 10 seconds, or the host's robots.txt Crawl-delay if longer, between requests for the same host.
run_plan.retries: None. A failed request counts as a failure. An HTTP 429 from the API stops the run (a harness fault, not a vendor result).
run_plan.robots: Every page must be allowed by its site's robots.txt for User-agent * and FirecrawlAgent before the run starts; a robots.txt answering 401, 403, 5xx or not at all counts as disallow.
run_plan.control: One direct request per page (plain HTTP GET, no rendering, user agent ScrapeToolsBench/1.0) shows which pages need rendering or unblocking. It is a reference, not a vendor.

firecrawl.settings_note: Defaults except: maxAge 0 and storeInCache false so every request fetches the page fresh (the default serves a cached copy up to 2 days old), onlyMainContent false so the whole page is checked, proxy pinned to its default 'auto' (retries with Firecrawl's enhanced proxy if the basic one fails, at no extra credit per its docs). No waitFor, no actions, no JSON format. Client timeout 90 s.

pricing.note: 1 credit per page scraped, including pages returned with an error status such as 403 or 404; 0 credits when no document is returned (billing docs). The enhanced proxy costs the same 1 credit. Monthly list prices; annual billing is cheaper but this site quotes monthly prices.

ruling_rule.question: Does Firecrawl earn a place in the ScrapeTools price comparison?
yes_only_if_all: R1 eligibility: it sells its own API on published monthly credit plans that state the credits a request uses (the home page's existing rule for its credit-plan vendors).
R2 reliability: at least 90% of requests to the general panel (static and js pages) succeed.
R3 billing: the credits the account's own counter shows for the run equal at most 1 credit per request sent, so the published price is what the measured pages cost.
R4 valid run: harness faults (API 429, our own network errors) stay under 5% of requests; otherwise no ruling is made from the run.
ruling_rule.not_criteria: Price rank. The comparison lists every eligible vendor sorted by cost, so a more expensive vendor still belongs if it meets R1-R3. The protected pair is reported but is not part of R2, because two pages are too few to rule on.
